chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the Dhuhr prayer until the sun set, and he had already prayed Asr. He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), or my father (peace be upon him), used to say: If he is able to pray it before the Maghrib time passes, he should begin with it; otherwise, he should pray Maghrib and then pray it (Dhuhr).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for making up Dhuhr prayer if one forgot it until sunset after praying Asr?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific scenario of 'Qada' (making up) Dhuhr after Asr has been prayed, establishing a priority between the missed obligatory prayer and the current time's prayer. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing the urgency of the current prayer time against the obligation of the missed one, ensuring neither is neglected. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of 'Nasiyan' (forgetfulness) in Al-Kafi, illustrating the practical application of prayer order in complex temporal overlaps.
